findings.title: Community text as restraint and boundary crossing
findings.claim: The revealed standard is presented as a norm that checks a community's practice, while the final label can also be heard as an image of something emerging from its enclosing shell when that norm is refused.
findings.mechanism: The two focus hkm occurrences carry the alıkoyup geri çevirme facet, and fasiqun carries the taze hurmanın kabuğundan çıkması facet. The wider supplied relations at 4:135 and 3:82 return through those same focus forms, so command and verdict read together as containment and boundary crossing.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus becomes more than a rule addressed to a named community: the reader can perceive both the norm's containing action and the visible movement of stepping outside it.
findings.containment: The plain command to judge by what God revealed remains intact. The shell image is a bounded collocational resonance, not a replacement gloss for fasiqun and not a claim that every use of the root has this sense.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and branch facets are supplied, but the reader-walk source is legacy_unbound and the connection rows provide target Arabic without target morphology; the relation is therefore retained with explicit qualification.

branch_activations.activation: The wider equity-and-desire contact makes the focus verb's restraint facet operate on communal practice rather than remain an isolated lexical possibility.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The revealed standard appears as an active restraint that turns practice back toward what has been entrusted.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not replace the ordinary judging sense or establish a complete legal theory from the wider relation.

findings.mechanism: The retrospective walk from 5:120 returns to the focus's command and conditional verdict, changing the local reading from an isolated rule or episode to a bounded relation between the received standard and the response to it.
findings.reader_payoff: The two halves of the ayah remain distinct yet become visibly contained within one larger frame of authority.
findings.containment: The later target text is not supplied in the packet, so this remains a retrospective exploratory relation rather than a claim about the full wording or architecture of 5:120.

findings.title: Revealed standard as corrective judgment
findings.claim: Judging by what is sent down is framed as corrective restraint: the entrusted text turns communal decision back toward the standard it received.
findings.mechanism: The focus hkm carrier meets the wide reader record's contrast between the revealed route and desire or sought ignorant judgment in 5:48-5:50. The supplied relations at 5:68, 2:213, and 4:105 extend the same criterion into book-community and dispute settings.
findings.reader_payoff: The command reads as an active correction of communal choice by received content, rather than as free-standing institutional power.
findings.containment: This retains the ordinary call to judge by the Gospel's revealed content. It does not settle every legal implication, and the separate adjudicative facet is preserved in its own finding.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is exact and the wider refs are supplied, but the reader-walk source is legacy_unbound and the connection rows explicitly lack target morphology; the interpretation remains qualified.

findings.title: Adjudication as dispute resolution
findings.claim: The focus verb can also present the revealed material as the basis by which disagreement among people is brought to a binding conclusion.
findings.mechanism: The focus hkm occurrences carry the adjudicative facet. Exact supplied targets at 34:26, 10:47, 2:213, and 4:135 show disputes gathered, settled, or judged with equity, returning that wider relation through the same focus verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the command as involving both a standard that restrains practice and a judgment that gives disagreement a settled form.
findings.containment: This adjudicative relation stands alongside the restraint reading. The target rows supply Arabic surface evidence and relation notes, not complete target morphology or a claim that every occurrence selects this facet.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus facet is supplied and the target Arabic is present, but the supporting connection rows lack target morphology and their relation notes remain nominations.

findings.title: Accountability under competing judgments
findings.claim: The nearby sequence makes the focus criterion accountable across competing routes: desire and a deliberately sought judgment of ignorance can redirect a route, and the focus names the refusal of its revealed standard.
findings.mechanism: The retrospective wide walk reads 5:48-5:50 as the later context that turns the focus's single community instruction into a test of what governs decision.
findings.reader_payoff: The conditional second half becomes a live fork in which the governing source of judgment matters, not merely the existence of a community or a text.
findings.containment: The record is legacy_unbound and supplies no independent lexical analysis for 5:48-5:50; this finding preserves the described before-and-after relation without claiming a complete pericope architecture.

epistemic.reason: The exact context references and changed-reading statement are supplied by a retrospective wide walk, while its source trust and lack of target morphology require qualification.

findings.title: Judgment as life-preserving containment
findings.claim: In attributed context, the focus command participates in a preventive-reparative operation: judgment restrains harm, protects life, arrests excess, and leaves a route toward repair.
findings.mechanism: The exact HFT trace places the focus hkm B001 occurrences against context occurrences identified at 5:30, 5:32, and 5:39 for killing, corruption, preserving life, excess, and reform; each attributed context role returns to the focus's revealed-judgment command.
findings.reader_payoff: The command becomes legible as part of an arc that interrupts harm and keeps restoration in view, while its ordinary scriptural-compliance reading remains available.
findings.containment: This is attributed contextual evidence. It does not invent glosses for the five unresolved context branches, turn 5:47 into a general criminal code, or remove the live alternative that the earlier material is legal background rather than the focus's immediate task.

epistemic.reason: The exact trace supplies context ayahs, word indices, roots, attributed roles, and a focus return, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and five context branch records remain unresolved; the finding is therefore retained as qualified attributed evidence.
